title: As-Salam, Peace itself
hook: Peace itself, the source of the greeting you've been saying since day one

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Quddus: Musa told to take off his sandals in the holy valley. Your line was the pure one. Did your cleared space stay clean and quiet? Day two hundred forty.

As-salamu 'alaykum. You learned it at the very start of this path. Peace be upon you. You've probably heard it a thousand times since: at a mosque door, on a phone call, in a shop, shouted across a parking lot. And the answer, wa 'alaykum as-salam, and upon you, peace. It's said so often it can shrink to a blur, salamlekum, the way good morning becomes morning. But the first word of that greeting isn't only a wish. It's one of the most beautiful names. Every time someone says it, a name of Allah passes between two people. Today: As-Salam, Peace itself.
screen: `AS-SALAMU 'ALAYKUM.` → `SAID A THOUSAND TIMES.` → `A NAME PASSING BETWEEN TWO PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: In the list at the end of al-Hashr, right after the King and the Holy One, Pickthall's translation has a single word: Peace. As-Salam. The root is s-l-m, and it means more than quiet. It means safe, sound, whole, unbroken. A salim heart is a sound one. Islam and Muslim come from the same root: surrender that brings wholeness. So as-Salam is the one who is whole and free from every harm, and the source of every wholeness anyone else has. Scholars have said the greeting means both: the peace of Allah be on you, and Allah, who is Peace, be with you. Peace wraps the prayer too. Every prayer ends by turning the head right and left and saying as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah. And Muslim records that after finishing, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would say: O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, Owner of majesty and honor. The Garden has the same name: in Surah Yunus, Allah calls to dar as-salam, the home of peace. And the Prophet made the greeting a path to love. In Sahih Muslim he said: you will not enter the Garden until you believe, and you won't believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you something that, if you do it, will make you love one another? Spread salam among yourselves. Not a slogan. A practice: say it to people you know and people you don't.
screen: `S-L-M — SAFE, SOUND, WHOLE.` · `THE PRAYER ENDS IN PEACE.` · `YOU ARE PEACE, AND FROM YOU IS PEACE.` · `SPREAD SALAM AMONG YOURSELVES.` · then, large: `PEACE IS HIS NAME.`

segments.voice: Sit, and turn your head gently to the right, the way the prayer ends. Think of someone on that side of your life, someone close. Silently wish them peace, whole and unbroken. Then turn to the left, and think of someone you find difficult, or someone you don't know at all, the cashier, the neighbor. Wish them peace too. Then face forward and breathe, and let the peace settle in the middle. If you pray, you can say, Allahumma anta s-Salam, O Allah, You are Peace. The bell holds the time.
As-Salam. Peace itself, the whole and the unharmed, the source of all peace, and the first word of the greeting. Today's word.
Your line: peace is his name. Today, greet one person deliberately, slowly, and mean every word of it, whether you say salaam, peace, or a real hello. Day two hundred forty.

screen: `DAY 240 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: AL-MU'MIN, THE GIVER OF SAFETY.`

howItsDone: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu 'alaykum and answer wa 'alaykum as-salam; every prayer ends by turning right and left with the greeting of peace, and after it many say Allahumma anta s-Salam wa minka s-salam.

original.note: Arabic: Peace, the whole and unharmed; a name of Allah and the first word of the greeting.

trapdoor: what you thought: salaam means hello.
what it means: Peace is a name of Allah, so the greeting passes His name between two people.
what a scholar hears: s-l-m, soundness and wholeness; 59:23; Muslim 591, anta s-Salam wa minka s-salam; Muslim 54, spread salam; 10:25, dar as-salam.

notes: Pickthall renders as-Salam in 59:23 as 'Peace'; the script names the single word only, with the verse cited as paraphrase.
Muslim 591 and 54 cited from memory; confirm.
The two scholarly readings of the greeting (the peace of Allah on you; Allah who is Peace be with you) should be confirmed.
The practice invites a greeting in any words, so non-Muslim listeners can take part.
